title: AI will make our children stupid
summary:
在近期种种显示西方文明正在衰落的迹象中，最令人沮丧的，莫过于智商水平明显下降的现实。曾经表明人类智商正持续提升的“弗林效应”，如今的逆转意味着我们可能正步入急剧的衰退。也许在不久的将来，当人们回望这个充斥着TikTok、《爱情岛》和扎克·波兰斯基的时代，反而会视其为一个尚存尊严与克制的时期。如果我们继续以当前的速度减少阅读，我们的孩子将继承一个真正意义上的“美丽新世界”：在那里，书籍会被看作晦涩难懂、甚至怪异反常的失落文明遗物。他们面对《莎士比亚全集》时的神情，大概就像黑猩猩盯着一部iPhone那般，茫然不解。

来源：The Critic；作者：David James and Carl Hendrick；原文发布时间：2025-12-22 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Of all the recent signs that Western civilization is circling the drain, the most depressing is the apparent decline in IQs. The so-called Flynn Effect once showed IQs rising steadily. Its reversal suggests we are heading for a steep decline. We may soon look back on this era of TikTok, Love Island and Zack Polanski as an age of dignity and restraint. If we stop reading at the current rate, our children will inherit a brave new world where books are viewed as arcane, even perverse, artifacts of a lost civilisation. They will stare at the Complete Works of Shakespeare much like a chimpanzee stares at an iPhone.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在近期种种显示西方文明正在衰落的迹象中，最令人沮丧的，莫过于智商水平明显下降的现实。曾经表明人类智商正持续提升的“弗林效应”，如今的逆转意味着我们可能正步入急剧的衰退。也许在不久的将来，当人们回望这个充斥着TikTok、《爱情岛》和扎克·波兰斯基的时代，反而会视其为一个尚存尊严与克制的时期。如果我们继续以当前的速度减少阅读，我们的孩子将继承一个真正意义上的“美丽新世界”：在那里，书籍会被看作晦涩难懂、甚至怪异反常的失落文明遗物。他们面对《莎士比亚全集》时的神情，大概就像黑猩猩盯着一部iPhone那般，茫然不解。

paragraphs.contentEn: When we started teaching we used to worry about the influence that cigarettes and alcohol, comics and television, were having on teenagers’ brains. Little did we know that those were our salad days, filled with such trifling trinkets of distraction compared to what we are facing now. It is axiomatic to say that attention is fundamental to learning, and strengthened attention can improve cognitive control, but over the last ten years we have seen attention spans weaken, reduced to a narrowness which makes teaching and learning not only increasingly difficult but actively resisted.
paragraphs.contentZh: 刚进入教育行业时，我们曾担心香烟、酒精、漫画和电视会对青少年的大脑产生不良影响。但当时并未意识到，那已是我们的黄金时代，与当下所面临的情况相比，当年的那些诱惑，不过是些无关紧要的琐碎干扰。可以说，注意力是学习的基本前提，强化注意力能提升认知控制能力。然而在过去十年里，我们目睹了学生注意力持续时间的不断萎缩，收缩到一种极其有限的程度，使得教学和学习不仅变得越来越困难，甚至开始遭到学生们的主动抵制。

paragraphs.contentEn: Intelligence is inherited, to some extent, but it also depends on our environments. Too many of our children struggle to focus in a way previous generations did not. While the causes are complex, mobile phones and social media are the primary culprits, and many children admit as much. But we may be at a turning point: last week Australia banned under-16s from ten of the world’s biggest social platforms. Watching this sociological stress test play out — particularly its enforcement and impact on education — will be fascinating, but already the downsides seem minimal. We have lived with the “great re-wiring” of adolescent brains for over a decade. The evidence of harm is compelling, as is the depressing data on the mental disorders that Zuckerberg et al have gifted to generations Z and Alpha.
paragraphs.contentZh: 智力在一定程度上由遗传决定，但也深受环境影响。如今，越来越多的孩子在集中注意力方面遇到困难，这是前几代人很少经历的情况。造成这一变化的原因固然复杂，但手机和社交媒体显然是主要推手，许多孩子自己也承认这一点。不过，我们或许正站在一个转折点上：上周，澳大利亚宣布禁止16岁以下的未成年人使用全球十大社交媒体平台。这项堪称社会学压力测试的禁令——其执行效果以及对教育的影响——尤其值得关注，但目前来看，这项禁令带来的负面后果似乎并不明显。十多年来，我们一直生活在青少年大脑被“大重构”的时代。关于这种变化所造成的伤害，证据已经相当充分，而扎克伯格等人馈赠给 Z 世代和 Alpha 世代的、有关心理健康问题的数据，同样令人沮丧。

paragraphs.contentEn: Yet there is a new boss in town. It is just as accessible as the old one, and owned by the same old behemoths (Meta, Google, Microsoft), but it is far more alarming. It arrives precision-designed to destroy whatever vestiges of cognition remain in the hollowed-out ruins of the teenage brain. It is, of course, AI. The threat that AI poses to intelligence is existential: it allows children to outsource their thinking entirely. Fundamental skills like mental arithmetic, memorising text, or reading a map could soon be obsolete as cognitive offloading becomes a normal way of working. We are fast becoming what educationalist Daisy Christodoulou calls a “stupidogenic” society. We are building a world where the phone isn’t just smarter than the chimpanzee holding it — it’s the only one of the two doing any thinking at all.
paragraphs.contentZh: 但如今，这块地盘上登场了一位新的掌控者。它和过去的技术一样触手可及，背后仍由那些老牌科技巨头（Meta、谷歌和微软）掌控，但带来的风险却更加令人不安。它的设计精准无比，目的就是要摧毁青少年那已被掏空的大脑中所残存的最后一点认知能力。这股力量，就是人工智能。人工智能对人类智力构成的是一种生存层面的威胁：它让孩子们可以将思考本身完全外包出去。随着认知卸载逐渐成为常态，心算、背诵文本、看懂地图这些基本技能，可能很快也会失去用武之地。我们正在迅速走向教育学者戴西·克里斯托多洛所说的“致蠢型社会”。在这样一个由我们亲手建构的世界里，手机不仅比握着它的黑猩猩更聪明——甚至成了两者之中唯一还在进行思考的一方。

paragraphs.contentEn: As Christodoulou argues, part of the problem is the technology, but it’s also the desire among people in positions of authority and influence, to embrace this Endarkenment. They believe that exams need to be adapted (read: abolished) in order to embrace AI. Of course, the opposite is true, and the fact is that at the very point that we need our brains more than ever — to be able to retain concentration so that we can learn and distinguish between what is real and what is AI slop — comes at the very same time we are voluntarily in the process of re-booting ourselves with a deeply flawed downgrade.
paragraphs.contentZh: 正如克里斯托多洛所指出的，技术固然是问题的一部分，但同样关键的是，那些掌握权柄与影响力的人，主动选择拥抱这种反启蒙的趋势。在他们看来，为了适应人工智能，考试制度需要调整（换句话说，就是被取消）。但事实正好相反，眼下，我们比任何时候都更需要仰赖自身心智——需要保持专注以学习新知、分辨什么是真实信息，什么只是人工智能生成的垃圾内容——却在此刻自愿启动了一场对自身认知进行有严重缺陷的系统降级重启。

paragraphs.contentEn: The danger here is the separation of process from “product”. In the eyes of the utilitarian tech-evangelist, the essay is simply a product, a sequence of words to be generated as quickly as possible. But the process of writing is itself constitutive of understanding. Writing is thinking. It is the act of retrieving knowledge, wrestling with syntax, and organising logic that forges understanding. When AI produces the final text, the student is the ventriloquist’s dummy, mouthing words that originated elsewhere. They possess the answer but lack the understanding of how it was derived, rendering them incapable of critiquing, adapting, or applying that knowledge in any novel context. We are also witnessing a kind of cognitive laziness which some of our institutions are actively encouraging. When universities tell students to “use AI responsibly” without defining what that actually means, they are licensing the very abdication they should be resisting.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这里真正的风险在于将“过程”与“产物”割裂开来。在功利至上的技术布道者眼中，文章不过是一件成品，是一串需要尽快生成的字符。但写作的过程本身，正是理解形成的过程。写作就是思考。这种调动知识储备、斟酌句法、组织逻辑的行为，才真正锻造了深度理解。一旦由人工智能来生成最终文本，学生就成了腹语师手中的木偶，只是在重复来自他处的词语。他们得到了答案，却不了解答案是如何得出的，因而也无法对这些知识进行批判、调整，或在任何新的情境中加以运用。与此同时，我们也正在见证一种思维惰性的扩散，而一些教育机构甚至在主动助长这种倾向。当高校在没有给出明确界定的情况下，只是笼统地要求学生“负责任地使用人工智能”时，实际上等同于为他们本应抵制的思考放弃行为开了绿灯。

paragraphs.contentEn: Ultimately, learning requires friction. It requires the uncomfortable sensation of not knowing, the strain of recall, and the cognitive demand that tech companies are seeking to eliminate. By smoothing away these difficulties with AI, we are not making our children smarter, or giving them “21st century skills”; we are turning them into passive consumers of synthetic intelligence, doomed to float on a sea of algorithmic slop they have neither the will nor the wit to navigate.
paragraphs.contentZh: 归根结底，学习本身需要阻力。它需要面对未知时的不适感，需要努力回忆时的紧张感，也需要科技公司正试图消除的那种认知负荷。用人工智能把这些困难一一抹平，并不会让孩子更聪明，也不会赋予他们所谓的“21世纪技能”；相反，我们是在将他们塑造成合成智能的被动消费者，使其注定漂浮在算法生成的垃圾信息之海中，既缺乏意愿，也缺乏能力去辨别和驾驭。
